svg.text: Mixture-of-Experts: Training Demands vs Inference Serving
Why MoE training introduces communication, gradient, and memory challenges absent during inference serving.
MoE Serving (Inference Lesson 35)
Read-Only Weights: 2 bytes/param (BF16) or 1 byte (FP8)
• Memory: Weights + KV cache; no optimizer or gradients.
• Execution: Forward pass only; no backpropagation.
• Routing: Router weights are static frozen parameters.
• Communication: Single forward All-to-All or TP All-Reduce.
• Bottleneck: Memory bandwidth for loading active expert weights.
Treated as a retrieval and batching problem.
MoE Training (AI Training Lesson 15)
Adam States for ALL Experts: 16 bytes/param
• Memory: Every expert (active or idle) requires 16 bytes.
• Execution: Forward + backward passes through dynamic routes.
• Routing gradients: Router weights require continuous backprop.
• Communication: Four All-to-All collectives per MoE layer.
• Stability: Router collapse, token dropping, and load imbalance.
A high-throughput interconnect and numerical stability challenge.
The Core Training Dilemma: MoE training provides the compute throughput of a smaller model (6 × N_active × D FLOPs)
while demanding the memory capacity (16 × N_total bytes) and cluster interconnect of a giant model.
